instruction_summary: Analysis-only re-analysis of 001's 2021->2025 era ladder: how FV effect size, peak edit-layer-as-fraction-of-depth, and head-localization concentration vary with scale/family/generation and the MHA->GQA shift; fit peak_layer ~ alpha*L + beta and restate Todd et al.'s claim for 2025 models.

steps.description: Read 001 per-model artifacts (consolidated.json, per-model head_localization.json and antonym_perf_v_heads.json) and 001's committed anchor values for GPT-J/NeoX; cross-checked the GPT-J anchor against the replication disk (per-seed argmax then mean reproduces 65.9% / peak_frac 0.361).

Assembled 6-rung master table and fit peak_layer = alpha*L + beta (OLS + through-origin) over all rungs and over the MHA subset; computed effect-size vs era/scale, concentration by architecture, induction enrichment ratios, #heads plateau as fraction of n_heads.
Built 3 figures reusing 001's palette/markers: effect-size-vs-era, peak-layer-vs-depth fit (headline), concentration-vs-family.

key_results.peak_layer_fit_MHA_through_origin: peak_layer = 0.30*L (alpha=0.30 ~ paper's L/3); peak-fraction 0.315 +/- 0.048 across GPT-J, NeoX, Llama-2, OLMo-2; residuals within +/-1.9 layers

peak_layer_fit_MHA_OLS.note: low R2 is a range artifact: MHA depths span only 28-44

peak_layer_fit_all_rungs_OLS.note: single depth-proportional rule collapses because GQA Qwen breaks it

key_results.effect_size_range: mean ZS FV 45.0-92.2% across 2021->2025; gap over no-FV baseline 42.7-86.9 pp

effect_size_vs_scale.verdict: weakly negative; family/pretraining dominates, not size

induction_enrichment_ratio_topK_over_all.verdict: persists directionally except OLMo-2; weakens sharply after GPT-J

numheads_plateau_k.verdict: ~10-head plateau holds for MHA; GQA needs proportionally ~2.5x more

comparison_to_original.followup: MHA alpha=0.30 (through origin), holds; all-rung single slope alpha=0.02 R2=0.00 (GQA breaks it)
comparison_to_original.source_file: paper.pdf (|L|/3 heuristic) + 001 consolidated.json per_task_peaklayer + head_localization.json n_layers
comparison_to_original.note: L/3 confirmed for MHA across 3 families; GQA Qwen drifts to ~0.6*L

comparison_to_original.quantity: GPT-J anchor mean ZS FV @ peak (3-task subset)
comparison_to_original.note: anchor unchanged; 002 adds no new measurement, only re-derivation
MHA->GQA shift roughly doubles the peak fraction
C5 signature preserved; GQA deeper/more diffuse
C13 weakens after GPT-J; breaks for OLMo-2
plateau holds for MHA; GQA needs ~2.5x more heads

deviations: No instruct rung: 001 skipped Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (gated), so the base-vs-instruct confound named in the instruction could not be tested; flagged, not worked around.
GPT-NeoX rung is antonym-only (single task) as inherited from 001; it enters the effect-size and peak-layer fits but has no concentration/induction/#heads data.
Qwen3 country-capital FV failed entirely (001); its spurious layer-0 'peak' is excluded from Qwen3's effective peak layer (0.542). The all-task value (0.361) is also recorded in derived_master.json.

Anchor values (GPT-J, NeoX) taken from 001's committed numbers rather than recomputed, to avoid method drift; independently cross-checked against the replication disk (GPT-J peak 65.87% ~ 001's 65.9%; peak_frac 0.361 exact; baseline within 0.3 pp).
n=6 rungs, single seed, bf16 (new models) vs fp16 (anchors) inherited from 001; scale/era trends have wide CIs (p~0.4-0.9), so reported as 'effect holds / no monotone trend', not precise slopes.
Low R2 on the MHA peak_layer~alpha*L OLS fit is a depth-range artifact (MHA L spans only 28-44); the robust statement is the tight peak-fraction cluster 0.315+/-0.05 ~ L/3.
